text: Binding starts a specific response. In muscle cells, insulin binding leads to an increase in glucose uptake: watch more glucose enter once insulin has bound. How the cell does that inside is a later topic; here you name the response. Liver cells carry the same insulin receptor, so they respond too, in their own way. A cell without a complementary receptor for insulin does not respond to it. So the blood broadcasts the message, and the receptors decide where it is acted on. That is why complementary shape matters.
